summary.headline: FY26 bookings rose 120% to INR 744 crores on Solano Gardens launch, while Q4 margins were hit by about INR 14 crores of one-off expenses.
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 bookings of INR 744 crores (up 120% YoY) and collections of INR 352.1 crores (up ~39%), driven by the Solano Gardens launch where 343 of 433 units sold for over INR 384 crores. Q4 FY26 booking value was INR 382.7 crores and collections INR 96.5 crores. Q4 profitability was dented by about INR 14 crores of one-time items (GST input write-off of ~INR 11 crores plus earlier-project costs). The company added ~INR 2,000 crores GDV through three Lucknow land parcels, two via LDA auctions, and guided to ~INR 4,000 crores total GDV across ongoing, unsold and yet-to-launch projects over 5 to 7 years.

financial_highlights.value: INR 60-64 crores, of which Imperia Phase 2 ~INR 47 crores

segments.name: Eldeco Solano Gardens (Lucknow)
segments.commentary: Launch phase sold 343 of 433 units, booking over INR 384 crores; mix of plots (50-60% margin), villas and group housing, with weighted average margin of about 35-40% per management. Around 75-80% of horizontal component absorbed; first multi-storied project expected in a couple of quarters to year-end.

segments.name: Imperia Phase 2
segments.commentary: Total turnover about INR 300 crores; ~INR 47 crores recognised in Q4 FY26 (70-80% of Q4 revenue). Management guides INR 130-150 crores recognition in FY27. Project substantially complete with completion certificate obtained; possession offered ahead of schedule.

segments.name: Eldeco Latitude 27
segments.commentary: Project value about INR 270-280 crores. Official handover commitment November 2027, with management hinting at possible earlier delivery, potentially within FY27; 4 of 5 towers in first phase, one tower lagging 6-9 months.

segments.name: Eldeco Trinity
segments.commentary: Bookings declined slightly in the quarter; sample flat ready and relaunch planned in about 3 weeks. Recent launches priced at about INR 8,000-11,000 per sq ft, above weighted average.

guidance_outlook: FY27 construction spend expected up 15-20% from FY26 INR 177.7 crores, to about INR 200 crores.
FY27 recognition from Imperia Phase 2 guided at INR 130-150 crores; management called these conservative and said recognition could come earlier.
FY27 margin outlook: EBITDA margin about 30-35% and PAT margin about 25%, driven by Imperia 2 recognition.
Big launches expected towards end of FY27 after approvals and RERA; no major launch in the next quarter, only small launches.
Total GDV across ongoing, unsold and yet-to-launch projects about INR 4,000 crores, expected to be sold over 5-7 years.
Management said the one-off expenses are cleared and no further one-offs are expected in coming quarters.
capex_capacity: Three Lucknow land parcels added in Q4 FY26 with GDV of about INR 2,000 crores and ~2 million sq ft saleable area, including two LDA auction parcels and a Shaheed Path parcel; launch expected towards end of FY27 subject to designs, approvals and RERA.
Solano Gardens has four parcels reserved for multi-storied group housing launches, to be rolled out over multiple years.
Management is considering replicating the Solano Gardens template at 2-3 more locations; Gorakhpur land talks ongoing with term sheets but nothing tied up.
Organic land aggregation continuing in 3-4 undisclosed locations; major business development deferred as hands are full for the next couple of quarters.
Latitude 27 has 5 towers; construction spend follows project timelines rather than sales pace.
demand_pricing: Management says demand in Lucknow is organic and not materially affected by geopolitics; a stock market slowdown could delay big purchases, and construction cost transmission is the bigger risk.
About 30-40% of collections are funded by home loans; management does not expect a rate reversal to change demand much.
Weighted average realisation per sq ft has risen sharply to around INR 6,500; management says new city-centric projects will push pricing higher, though prices are stagnating generally.

Recognised revenue can exceed delivered area: Q4 revenue of about INR 64 crores against 18,530 sq ft and 26 units delivered, because revenue is recognised on possession offered and collections completed under Ind AS 115.
Management sees supply, not demand, as the constraint in Lucknow, citing fragmented and disputed land.
Management said the UP urban development policy (February) eases FAR and approvals and is positive; it sees limited impact from possible entry of national players.

qa_highlights.question: What margins do plotted and villa projects carry versus the wider portfolio, and what margins are expected next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Plotted margins are 50-60%; Solano's weighted average including villas is about 35-40%. FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 30-35% and PAT about 25%, driven by Imperia 2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margins fall and what was the one-off expense?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 14 crores one-time costs, including ~INR 11 crores GST input written off and earlier-project costs, hit EBITDA and PAT in Q4 and FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Imperia Phase 2 will be recognised in FY27 and what is unsold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management projects INR 130-150 crores recognition in FY27; total project turnover about INR 300 crores, with the balance dependent on customer possession timing.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Imperia 2 recognition slow when the project is complete?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised only when control passes; customers who have not taken possession keep paying instalments, so recognition depends on their possession timing. Management said numbers are conservative.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 launch plan and how much GDV can be monetised?
qa_highlights.answer: Big launches are expected towards end-FY27 after approvals and RERA; no major launch in the next quarter. Management pointed to the ~INR 4,000 crores GDV over 5-7 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the construction budget for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 spend was about INR 177 crores (vs INR 150-160 crores prior year); FY27 expected about INR 200 crores, up 15-20%, rising as more projects launch.

risks_watch: Q4 margin dilution from one-offs and reliance on Imperia Phase 2 recognition timing for FY27 earnings.
Revenue recognition depends on customer possession timing; Imperia 2 recognition could slip.
Big FY27 launches are dependent on approvals and RERA registration; no major launch expected in the next quarter.
Construction cost inflation is seen as the bigger macro risk than demand.
Competition from national players may rise after the UP urban development policy; Trinity bookings dipped and relaunch is pending.
Latitude 27 earlier-than-November 2027 handover is not committed; official date remains November 2027.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, execution and the pipeline, with management saying Imperia 2 was completed ahead of schedule. Cautious and deliberately conservative on revenue timing and FY27 launches, repeatedly deferring specifics to the next quarter and declining to give exact figures.
key_quotes: So FY26 has been a milestone year for EHIL with record bookings and collections, a standout launch and most importantly, a meaningful expansion of our growth pipeline that significantly enhances our medium-term visibility.
The demand supply gap is so skewed that we don't even worry about demand anymore. We just worry about supply.
So, obviously, numbers that we are putting out are always on the conservative side. It could be earlier.
